title: Position-Returning EBNF Recognizers
description: See how returning the stopping position (or None) lets a recognizer report where a match ended.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: `recognize_integer(text, pos=0)` starts at index `pos`. It returns `None` on line 8 if the required first digit is missing. Otherwise, it returns the integer index `pos` on line 12 where the `{ digit }` loop stopped, rather than a boolean.

`check(rule, text)` calls `end = rule(text)` and checks `ok = end == len(text)` on line 16. When `ok` is `False`, line 18 prints `(stopped at {end})` so you can distinguish a missing required piece (`None`) from an unconsumed suffix.
Compare returning `None` on line 8 with returning `pos` on line 12: returning an index lets a caller know how much of `text` the rule consumed.

steps.question: When `check(recognize_integer, t)` runs on `"-"` and `"4a"` on lines 21-22, what value does `recognize_integer` return for each (`end`), and why are both rejected?
steps.answer: For `"-"`, `pos` advances to `1` on line 6 and line 8 returns `None` (`stopped at None`) because no digit follows `'-'`. For `"4a"`, the `while` loop stops at `'a'` and line 12 returns `1` (`stopped at 1`), which does not equal `len("4a")` (`2`).

steps.description: Lines 20-22 run `check(recognize_integer, t)` on seven test inputs, and lines 24-39 provide the starter stub for `recognize_identifier`.
While checking `''`, `pos >= len(text)` (`0 >= 0`) is `True` on line 7, so line 8 returns `None`.
